Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

This writ petition has been filed, inter alia, for the following reliefs :-
"i) Issue a writ order or direction into the nature of mandamus directing the respondent authorities that they will not interfere into the peaceful running of shop nos.796 & shop no.56 of the petitioners, situated at Main Bazar, near Bus Stand,
Bahadurgarh, Garhmukeshwar, District Hapur.
ii) Issue a writ order or direction in the nature of mandamus commanding the respondent No. 2 that he will decide the representation dated 02.07.2019 made by the petitioners."

sentences.text:
Petitioners' claim to have individual certificate of Registration under Food Safety and Standards Act,
2006 (hereinafter referred as to 'the Act of 2006') for conducting business of retail meat shop (meat and meat products including poultry) which is valid up to 09.08.2024.

Shri Awadhesh Kumar Mishra, learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that petitioners have valid registration for retail meat shop (meat and meat products including poultry) but the respondents - District Administration and District Food and Safety Officer are unnecessary forcing the petitioners to stop their business.

Learned counsel for the petitioners further submitted that the respondents have illegally stopped their vehicle which was used for transporting the meat as well as threaten the petitioners to stop their business.
The act of the respondent is infringing the petitioners' right to run their business as provided under Article 19 of the Constitution of India.

Learned counsel for the petitioners has also relied upon the judgment passed by the Apex Court in the case of State Of Gujarat vs Mirzapur Moti Kureshi Kassab reported at 2005 8 SCC 535, as well as the judgment passed by the Division Bench of this Court in the matter of Mohd. Mustafa & others vs. Union of India Thru.

sentences.text: Secretary Ministry Health & Family Welfare in order to show that the petitioners' right of food business cannot be disturbed without due process of law.

Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respondents submitted that the petitioners have approached the District Magistrate, Hapur by submitting an application dated 02.07.2019 wherein they have mentioned that the District Administration is not permitting them to slaughter at their shop as well as petitioners may be permitted to carry the meat from the slaughter houses situated at Rampur, Ghaziabad and Meerut even in a vehicle which is an non-air conditional vehicle.
It is further submitted that the registration/license for food business are provided under Chapter 2 of the Food Safety and Standards (licensing and registration of food business) Regulations, 2011.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Schedule 4 part 1 of (Regulation No. 2.1.1(2)) provide measures to be adopted by the such registration holder.
One of the condition is to keep the food in hygienic manner.
No permission has been granted to the petitioner for slaughtering.

Learned counsel further submits that the petitioners have to follow Regulations prescribed under the Regulations 2011 as well as notification issued by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) time to time.

sentences.text: Considered the submissions made by the rival parties and perused the records.

The Registration issued to the petitioners is regulated under the provisions of the Act, 2006 as well as Regulations 2011 issued under the Act which provides measures to be adopted by the registration holder.

For reference, relevant part of the Regulations (Schedule 4 part 1) is quoted hereinafter :-
"SANITARY AND HYGIENIC REQUIREMENTS FOR FOOD MANUFACTURER/
PROCESSOR/HANDLER The place where food is manufactured, processed or handled

shall comply with the following requirements:
1. The premises shall be located in a sanitary place and free from filthy surroundings and shall maintain overall hygienic environment.
All new units shall set up away from environmentally polluted areas.

2. The premises to conduct food business for manufacturing should have adequate space for manufacturing and storage to maintain overall hygienic environment.
3. The premises shall be clean, adequately lighted and ventilated and sufficient free space for movement.
4. Floors, Ceilings and walls must be maintained in a sound condition.
They should be smooth and easy to clean with no flaking paint or plaster.
5. The floor and skirted walls shall be washed as per requirement with an effective disinfectant the premises shall be kept free from all insects.
No spraying shall be done during the conduct of business, but instead fly swats/ flaps should be used to kill spray flies getting into the premises.
Windows, doors and other openings shall be fitted with net or screen, as appropriate to make the premise insect free
The water used in the manufacturing shall be potable and if required chemical and bacteriological examination of the water shall be done at regular intervals at any recognized laboratory.
6. Continuous supply of potable water shall be ensured in the premises.
In case of intermittent water supply, adequate storage arrangement for water used in food or washing shall be made.
7. Equipment and machinery when employed shall be of such design which will permit easy cleaning.
Arrangements for cleaning of containers, tables, working parts of machinery, etc. shall be provided.
8. No vessel, container or other equipment, the use of which is likely to cause metallic contamination injurious to health shall be employed in the preparation, packing or storage of food.

(Copper or brass vessels shall have proper lining).
9.
All equipments shall be kept clean, washed, dried and stacked at the close of business to ensure freedom from growth of mould/ fungi and infestation.
10. All equipments shall be placed well away from the walls to allow proper inspection.
11. There should be efficient drainage system and there shall be adequate provisions for disposal of refuse.
12. The workers working in processing and preparation shall use clean aprons, hand gloves, and head wears.
13. Persons suffering from infectious diseases shall not be permitted to work.
Any cuts or wounds shall remain covered at all time and the person should not be allowed Farukh And Another vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 23 July, 2019

14. All food handlers shall keep their finger nails trimmed, clean and wash their hands with soap, or detergent and water before commencing work and every time after using toilet.
Scratching of body parts, hair shall be avoided during food handling processes.

15. All food handlers should avoid wearing, false nails or other items or loose jewellery that might fall into food and also avoid touching their face or hair.
16.
Eating, chewing, smoking, spitting and nose blowing shall be prohibited within the premises especially while handling food.
17. All articles that are stored or are intended for sale shall be fit for consumption and have proper cover to avoid contamination.
18. The vehicles used to transport foods must be maintained in good repair and kept clean.
19. Foods while in transport in packaged form or in containers shall maintain the required temperature.
20.Insecticides/disinfectants shall be kept and stored separately and away from food manufacturing/storing/handling areas.

It is evident from the certificate of registration issued to the petitioners that they have been granted permission for the business of retail meat shop (meat and meat products including poultry) only and no permission has been granted for slaughtering.

The representation dated 02.07.2019 submitted by the petitioners is for the purpose of granting permission for slaughtering at the shop and to permit for bringing meat from the slaughter houses in an non-air conditional vehicle.

Both the said requests are contrary to the conditions of Registration and Regulations as mentioned above as well as judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Laxmi Narain Modi v. Union of India reported at (2014) 2 SCC 417 wherein certain directions have been passed to modernize the slaughter houses.

entities.text: Laxmi Narain Modi v. Union of India reported at (2014) 2 SCC 417
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: For the reasons recorded above, the petitioners have failed to make out a case to grant any relief under the Writ Jurisdiction of this Court.
The petitioners are bound to follow the conditions laid down in Regulations dealing with Registration.
The writ petition is misconceived, and is accordingly, dismissed.
